A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same critical-batch-size study. The complete main texts, figures, tables and Appendices A–G are readable and matchable; v4's shorter length reflects layout consolidation rather than missing material.

before.justification: v3 reports original C4 language-model training experiments, critical-batch-size scaling results, scheduler comparisons and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including experiments with models ranging from 85M to 1.2B parameters.

M1.justification: The model architectures, Adam training procedure, constant learning rate with exponential weight averaging, and CBS measurement procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same C4 language-modeling coverage and experimental scenarios. No datasets, tasks or evaluated domains are added or removed.

E2.justification: The scheduler comparisons retain cosine, WSD and schedule-free optimization in Figures 2 and 9. The added Adam convergence citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Target-loss selection, the 20% CBS overhead criterion, training budgets, validation cadence and hyperparameter grids remain identical. Tables 1–5 retain the same settings despite relocation.

E4.justification: The context-length, width/depth, warmup, EWA, weight-decay, Adam and small-batch analyses are retained. Repositioning the appendix figures introduces no new ablation or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged, including Appendix D's variance estimates for different validation-set sizes. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The reported losses, optimization-step curves, CBS scaling fits and forecasts are unchanged, including the appendix results and Tables 6–7. Moved figures retain their original plotted content.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the condition in the variance-dominated discussion from b < a to b > a, resolving a mathematical inconsistency with Corollary 2. The formal theorem and corollary statements and Appendix G proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: CBS scales primarily with data size, depends weakly on model size, and can be studied using constant learning rates with EWA.

C2.justification: The explanation following Corollary 2 now correctly associates variance-dominated behavior and the corresponding batch-size tradeoff with b > a. Empirical interpretations and existing applicability qualifications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameter tables, evaluation instructions, A100 hardware disclosure, OLMo framework information and the code-access link are retained. Added citations provide context without changing reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: v4 adds Zhang et al. (2022), Adam can converge without any modification on update rules. Appendices A and D also explicitly connect existing warmup and hyperparameter choices to Porian et al. (2024); the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized punctuation, capitalization, tense and caption-wording edits, plus brief additions connecting experimental choices to prior work. Section ordering and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The appendix layout is consolidated: Figure 8 moves to page 20, Figure 12 is placed beside text, Figures 13–14 share page 23, and Tables 2–3 share page 25. Figures and tables retain their content and numbering.

improvement.justification: v4 fixes the misleading b < a condition in Section 4.2, bringing the explanation into agreement with Corollary 2 and its existing proof. Added attribution improves context for experimental choices, and appendix consolidation preserves the evidence. These are limited improvements; the methods, empirical support and central claims remain unchanged.
